name: McALLISTER, the Hon. Jennifer (Jenny) Ryll

headline.note: Official records establish NSW ministerial-adviser service from 2002 to 2006, NSW public service from 2006 to 2010 and AECOM employment from 2010 to 2015. Primary NSW records identify senior climate-policy roles, while public biographies describe three AECOM title phases. None of the reviewed sources establishes hours, leave, exact transition dates or substantive full-time status. Political staff, party office, candidacy, campaigning, elected office, study and nonprofit activism are excluded; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary synthesis, citing a public professional profile, records University of Queensland study from 1992 to 1995 with a politics and government major. Degree completion, load and any employment overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts (First Class Honours) student in political economy, politics and government
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies list the University of Sydney BA(Hons); secondary synthesis reports graduation in 1996 and the fields and honours result. Commencement, load and work overlap are not published in the sources reviewed. Public professional profile now indexed with Sydney1996–1997, conflicting with secondary1996 graduation. Existing graduation marker retained pending original university conferral record; neither range determines employment hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member; conference/committee member, policy participant and election-campaign director
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary synthesis reports National Policy Committee service in 1998–2000 and 2006–2007, NSW State Conference membership from 1999, NSW Administrative Committee membership from 2000 and direction of several election campaigns. It does not establish remuneration, hours or a continuing employment relationship. NSW Labor’s own biography dates initial party membership in Queensland to 1992, before the later NSW positions.
career_spells.counting_note: Party membership, committees and campaign organisation are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: A public professional biography states that McAllister advised federal MP Tanya Plibersek before joining NSW Environment Minister Bob Debus in 2002. The official parliamentary occupation list omits this role, and the reviewed sources do not provide dates, title, payroll entity, hours or leave.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal political-staff work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary political biography records McAllister as Labor's Richmond candidate at the 10 November 2001 federal election. Preselection date, campaign remuneration, hours and overlap with any employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of Bob Debus, NSW Minister for the Environment
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen and current parliamentary biographies record NSW environment-minister adviser service from 2002 to 2006. In a later Senate speech McAllister described four years working for Bob Debus. Exact appointment and cessation dates, payroll entity, hours, leave and the transition from the Plibersek office are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: State ministerial political-staff work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: NSW Department of Environment and Climate Change / Department of Environment, Climate Change and Water
career_spells.role: Director, Climate Change Policy and Programs Group; later Director, Climate Change, Air and Noise
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary biographies give NSW public service from 2006 to 2010. A NSW parliamentary climate-impact report identifies McAllister as Director of the Climate Change Policy and Programs Group at an October 2008 committee briefing, providing a dated observation within the role; the department's 2009–10 annual report identifies her as Director of Climate Change, Air and Noise. Agency restructures, exact title dates, appointment basis, hours and leave remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The employer was government-controlled, but year-only boundaries and missing substantive full-time evidence prevent a public-sector duration.

career_spells.role: Strategic Adviser, Water and Climate; Associate Director
career_spells.evidence_note: Official profiles record AECOM service beginning in 2010; member and ministerial biographies identify AECOM as a global infrastructure firm. Secondary synthesis describes this first title phase through 2013, but title-phase boundaries were not established by a contemporaneous employer record. Exact dates, hours, leave and transition from the NSW department are unresolved. Contemporaneous January 2011 AECOM report identifies her as Associate Director and reviewer, resolving a title omitted from the secondary sequence and identifying legal entity/ABN. Whether Associate Director was concurrent corporate grade or a separate title phase is unresolved. Final-report authorisation is an observed work milestone, not start/end of employment.
career_spells.counting_note: AECOM was a private employer, but the role title and year range do not establish a countable full-time interval.

career_spells.evidence_note: This internal AECOM title phase is reported by secondary synthesis within the official 2010–2015 AECOM interval. Exact change date, hours, leave and whether duties overlapped the preceding or following title are not established by the reviewed sources. AECOM’s June 2013 Lower Hunter report independently credits her review work and legal employer, but does not assign the Technical Director title or establish when the internal change occurred.
career_spells.counting_note: A senior private-sector title does not by itself establish substantive full-time work or exact duration.

career_spells.role: Managing Director, Water and Urban Development; member of the Australia and New Zealand executive
career_spells.evidence_note: The official AECOM interval ends in 2015. Secondary synthesis reports this title and ANZ executive membership from 2014 until resignation to enter the Senate. The May endpoint is bounded by Senate commencement, not evidence of the employment cessation day; hours, leave and the campaign/party-office overlap remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The private employer is established, but seniority and apparent continuity do not substitute for hours, exact boundaries and leave evidence.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official and ministerial biographies record national presidency from 2011 to 2015; secondary chronology supplies the 1 July 2011 commencement and 17 June 2015 successor announcement. The role overlapped all three AECOM title phases and briefly overlapped Senate service. Remuneration and workload are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: NSW Labor biography dates founding to 2003 and inaugural convenorship through 2007. Subsequent activism end is unknown, so 2007 is not treated as cessation of all participation. Pay, hours and legal form remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party-network activity excluded; founding/convenorship does not establish separate full-time employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current government biographies record Senate service from 6 May 2015. Shadow, assistant-ministerial, ministerial, committee and party-room responsibilities are nested within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Walk Against the War Coalition / Labor member liaison
career_spells.evidence_note: NSW Labor biography reports work connecting party members to the coalition in 2002. Exact boundaries, pay and hours unspecified; no operational employer inferred.

career_spells.employer: Community and Public Sector Union — North Coast office
career_spells.evidence_note: Crikey public index describes the Richmond candidate as CPSU organiser, without reliable employment boundaries, hours or location.2015 IPA table instead marks no union background. Role retained as a specifically attributed unresolved report, not a verified full-time interval. A directly readable Crikey article dated 11 November 2001 places the reported organiser position in the CPSU North Coast office in the Richmond-candidacy context. This contemporaneous account strengthens the location and 2001 activity evidence but gives neither commencement nor cessation; dates remain null rather than converting publication into a job boundary. The contrary 2015 classification and missing original union record remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary executive table gives1994 secretary role. Remuneration, load and exact term need original student-union evidence; not an employment inference.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

research_notes: The official three-employer sequence is preserved, while primary NSW records add role titles within the 2006–2010 public-service interval.
AECOM is classified as private enterprise. Its internal title phases are displayed from public secondary synthesis, but no title is used to infer full-time status.
The Tanya Plibersek adviser role is retained as a lead from a public professional profile even though the official parliamentary occupation list begins with the Bob Debus role.
ALP presidency overlaps AECOM employment and briefly overlaps Senate service; party office is excluded rather than treated as a competing employment interval.
No public or private full-time total is calculated because hours, leave and exact transition dates remain unsupported.

2026-10-01 follow-up adds primary AECOM project evidence, legal entity/ABN and Associate Director title observed 21 January 2011; June 2013 review credit is not a title-transition date. NSW Labor resolves LEAN founding/convenorship and earlier party membership and anti-war organising.

Searched AECOM appointments and reports, NSW annual report/UN climate delegation records, first-speech and public professional profiles, full-time and leave wording. LinkedIn returned 999; UN PDF timed out; ASU conference-profile download failed. The NSW annual report remains a title source, not an individual hours record. Unrelated UK travel/teaching profiles were excluded. Graduation and party-presidency inconsistencies retained as follow-up gaps; no hours inferred from seniority or project credits.

Second follow-up2October2026 adds attributed CPSU organiser and student-union secretary roles and explicit Sydney study conflict. Employer-targeted AECOM searches and personal full-/part-time searches did not resolve employment load or phase boundaries; US realtor and UK teaching/travel profiles excluded as different people. The CPSU report is a new union-archive lead, not proof of employment in2006 or2001. No totals calculated.

3 October 2026 targeted follow-up found the directly readable 2001 Crikey account and resolved the reported CPSU office as North Coast, without fabricating start/end dates. University archive search found Semper Floreat 1994 issue 1 at https://espace.library.uq.edu.au/view/UQ%3A243944/SF_1994_Issue1.pdf with an indexed first-person student-union committee contact by McAllister, but original PDF returned 403 Forbidden; not retried or treated as verified secretary/pay evidence. University of Sydney targeted search did not resolve conferral. Next useful evidence is original CPSU North Coast staff records, accessible original UQU executive records and Sydney conferral records; avoid repeating broad AECOM/title and generic hours searches.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 refines the existing primary NSW parliamentary source: footnote and committee minutes place McAllister's Director, Climate Change Policy and Programs Group observation at an October2008 briefing. This does not establish appointment boundaries, hours or leave. Exact AECOM and ALP term searches did not resolve remaining transitions; the University of Sydney repository was robots-blocked and not bypassed.
open_questions: What were the exact appointment dates, payroll entities, hours and leave for the Tanya Plibersek and Bob Debus adviser roles?
What were the exact NSW department appointment dates, classifications, title transitions, hours and leave from 2006 to 2010?
Can contemporaneous AECOM records confirm the three titles, exact change dates, employment status, hours, leave and 2015 cessation date?
Did the 2001 Richmond campaign or later campaign-director work involve remuneration, and what paid work overlapped it?
What were the dates, legal form, remuneration and workload of LEAN activity and the ALP national presidency?
Did AECOM work continue after Senate commencement on 6 May 2015, or end earlier during preselection/casual-vacancy preparations?
Was AECOM Associate Director a corporate grade concurrent with Strategic Adviser, and what dates distinguish the three subsequent title phases?
Can original party election/term records reconcile presidency start/end dates in secondary infobox versus narrative (July/November 2011 and June/July 2015)?
What work or study occurred between university completion and the first known Plibersek role; can 1996/1997 graduation accounts be reconciled?
Can CPSU North Coast contemporary staff records confirm the reported organiser role around the 2001 Richmond candidacy, establish dates/pay/hours, and reconcile the 2015 contrary classification?
Can original UQU records confirm secretary term and paid status, and Sydney conferral records resolve1996 versus1997?
